exposure: Placental location at mid-trimester (anterior, posterior, or lateral)
cohort: The study included 474 pregnant women with singleton gestations between 18-24 weeks.
finding: Lateral placentation at mid-trimester was significantly associated with adverse maternal outcomes (earlier gestational age at delivery, increased preterm labour, gestational hypertension, preeclampsia) and fetal outcomes (IUGR, lower mean birth weight).
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were significantly higher in women with lateral placentation.
